day_shape: 80 items dominated by a US–Iran clash in the Strait of Hormuz with US strikes after a tanker incident, a revised US-Gulf UN draft resolution, State Dept sanctions on Iran-aligned Iraqi oil networks, and Pezeshkian's confirmation he met new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

threads.label: Hormuz clash and US strikes on Iran
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported US strikes on Iran following a Strait of Hormuz clash with Trump saying the ceasefire holds, while CENTCOM posted imagery of USS George H.W. Bush operating with 20+ warships enforcing a blockade. Defa Press and IRIB claimed Iran's navy hit US destroyers with cruise missiles and drones after alleged aggression on two Iranian tankers near Fujairah, with Khamenei's office vowing Iran would 'secure' the Gulf.

threads.label: UN Security Council Hormuz resolution
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported the US is urging support for a UNSC resolution demanding Iran halt attacks and mining of the Strait, with diplomats expecting a Russia-China veto. Al Jazeera, cited by IRIB and Defa Press, said a revised US-Gulf draft removed Chapter 7 references; Russia's UN delegation rejected 'unbalanced narratives,' and Iran's envoy Irvani told a UN press conference Iran supports freedom of navigation.

threads.label: US sanctions and Iraq oil networks
threads.summary: The State Department announced sanctions on Iran-aligned actors said to be exploiting Iraqi oil to fund Iranian regional activities, while OFAC published Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations General Licenses S and T in the Federal Register. Times of Israel also reported the US is hoping to resume Hormuz naval escorts while awaiting Iran's response to a peace offer.

threads.label: IDF operations in Lebanon and Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF said it dismantled a 30-metre Hezbollah tunnel and 200+ infrastructure sites in southern Lebanon and has killed 220+ Hezbollah operatives in recent weeks, including Radwan Force commander Ahmed Ali Balout, while cancelling northern events over revenge-attack concerns. Times of Israel reported Hamas chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya's son was killed in an IDF Gaza City strike, and Jerusalem Post reported Hamas operatives are being trained in Turkey.

threads.label: Mojtaba Khamenei succession signalling
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel reported President Pezeshkian said he met new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not appeared publicly since his appointment. Khamenei's office Telegram channel released Pezeshkian's account of the meeting and a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei calling for mutual support among Iranians.

threads.label: Iran domestic strain after strikes
threads.summary: Iran International reported a global internet shutdown is forcing Iranians onto distrusted domestic apps, 27,000 workers at Mobarakeh Steel remain in limbo after missile strikes paralysed production, and a think tank flagged possible new fortifications at the Pickaxe Mountain tunnel complex near Natanz. IRIB said grade 7–10 exams will be held in person pending state security council approval, and WFP reported 34,818 people assisted in Iran in April.

threads.label: Iran-linked plots and arrests abroad
threads.summary: Times of Israel cited the FBI saying the Austin bar shooter was motivated by support for Iran but acted alone, and Iran International reported German intelligence officials privately warn Iran-linked attack risks in Germany are more serious than publicly stated. Jerusalem Post reported a third arrest, a Portsmouth man, over the Finchley Reform Synagogue arson attempt linked to a wave of attacks on London Jewish, Israeli and Iranian dissident sites.

events.title_en: Russia's opposition to the anti-Iran resolution
events.summary_en: Russia's opposition to the anti-Iran resolution Russia's delegation to the UN: Moscow rejects any attempt to impose unbalanced narratives against Iran without considering the motives and causes of the crisis. Ensuring the security of maritime passage in the Persian Gulf region is closely linked to ending current conflicts and stopping all military operations. We warn that the adoption of biased resolutions may lead to a new wave of tensions in the Middle East. Russia has asked Security Council members to refrain from introducing resolutions with confrontational approaches while avoiding escalation.
